edges.act_citation_note:
CORRECTED 2026-08-01. This station carried `act_citation = "not-found"` from the
day it was drawn until the missal acquisition audit read the decree. The
correction, and why the error was made, are both worth keeping.

THE DECREE EXISTS AND HAS NOW BEEN READ, at page 2 of the Vatican typical
edition, in the exact facsimile this repository already had registered. Opening,
with the OCR damage of that text layer reproduced (`rubricanim`, `i960`):

  DECRETUM
  Novo rubricanim corpore, a Summo Pontifice Ioanne XXIII, Motu proprio
  << Rubricarum instructum >> diei 23 iulii anno i960 approbato posteroque die
  a Sacra Rituum Congregatione promulgato, vix fieri non potuit quin eadem
  Sacra Rituum Congregatio novam Missalis romani editionem, ad dictum
  rubricarum codicem plane accommodatam, pararet.

Operative clause: `hinc est quod praesens Vaticana Missalis romani editio uti
<< typica >> declaratur`. Dateline: `Romae, ex aedibus Sacrae Rituum
Congregationis, die 23 iunii 1962`, subscribed `A. M. Card. LARRAONA, S. R. C.
Praefectus` and `Henricus Dante, S. R. C. a secretis`.

So the incipit `Novo rubricarum corpore`, which this file expressly declined to
promote because it was known only from a report, is now read from the book.

WHY THE ERROR WAS MADE, because it is instructive and not careless. This
tracer's corpus is seven Internet Archive OCR text layers, and its 1962 witness
is the BENZIGER printing, which carries a New York imprimatur and not the
Vatican decree. The statement `only three occurrences of DECRETUM in 136,068
lines` was true of that scan. What was false was recording the result in a field
that reads as a claim about the repository -- because the repository held the
decree, in a passage record dated 2026-07-25, six days before this file was
written:
`passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.decretum-sacrae-rituum-congregationis-1962`,
states `verified`, locus `front matter, artifact PDF p. 2`.

Two records of one fact, in one tree, never compared. guidance/the-shape.md
section 2. `act_citation` is `cited-externally` rather than `cited-in-corpus`
because the decree stands in the Vatican typical edition, which is not a witness
of this file's corpus; the corpus is unchanged and its own negative result
stands as reported.
edges.parent_basis:
Two lines of descent, both on the same line of the rite: the reformed Holy Week
of 1955 and the code of rubrics of 1960. Neither alone accounts for the book.
edges.reception_basis:
The merge is drawn because the reception is visible in the book itself, to the
letter, and not inferred from the fact that both acts precede it.

From the 1955 side: section 9 of Maxima redemptionis, fixing the Vigil at
midnight, is reproduced word for word in the witness. The Acta print it at
aas-47-1955 51915-51921 and the book prints it at benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962
40203-40212. An act and a book agreeing letter for letter is a reception shown.

From the 1960 side: the Code of Rubrics is printed entire in the same book's
front matter, from benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 1276, with its promulgating decree
at 1235-1272 above it; and its renaming of the Introit is then carried through
into the Palm Sunday propers at 35155.

Where a reception cannot be shown like that, this file draws no merge, and
`act-history check` refuses any act with more than one parent that does not carry
this field.

cited.basis: Both readings quoted above, from the witnesses' own text layers; the act that stands between them was not found.
cited.note:
The witnesses differ and the act is not established. The pre-1955 books print
`Oremus et pro perfidis Judaeis` (missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 36442, pustet-1862
32769-32770); the 1962 witness prints `Oremus et pro Iudaeis` under a numbered
title `8. PRO CONVERSIONE IUDAEORUM` (benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 39247, 39252),
and a whole-file search of it for `perfid` returns nothing. The removal is
commonly attributed to John XXIII in 1959; no instrument for it was found in
this corpus and none is asserted from memory, so no station carries it and the
unit's state after this act is not established rather than assumed unchanged.

before.name: Rubrica

cited.basis: The readings quoted on the unit and above; no instrument was found for the change.
cited.note:
Same case again, and the third face of it. The pre-1955 rubric forbids the
kneeling that every other solemn prayer has; the 1962 witness prints `Oremus.
Flectamus genua. Levate.` at benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 39279 and carries no
such rubric. The two pre-1955 witnesses also disagree with each other about the
rubric's wording, with no act between them, which is why this unit could not be
established even before the 1962 witness was read.

cited.basis:
The witness gives each of the nine solemn prayers a numbered title, which the
pre-1955 witnesses do not print at all: benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 38786, 38865,
38939, 38993, 39073, 39126, 39197, 39247, 39288. Recorded as an addition at this
station because that is where it becomes visible, and it is deliberately not
attributed to the 1955 decree, whose text says nothing about titling the prayers.
